items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: I had a boy by the name of Joe Valadie. He was a nice trumpet player... I wouldn't fool with him. I wouldn't, because I knew he would have been too good a trumpet player if he had stayed and took what I wanted to give him.

ctx.x: You taught all the different instruments, the instruments, clarinet too? Yeah, clarinet and everything.

Clarinet, violin, and uh. Well you played violin for a while. Yeah, I played a little bit. Did you play much on the others? On the others ones, yeah. Trumpet, yeah. I played trumpet and lots and bass fiddle, bass drum, bass horn. I never, you know, kept them for a regular, but I had to know them. Sure. You know, I had to know them. So. Yeah. That's it. So I just kept on, got them all down, worked out. And I got some good, I put some good bands together. I want to sing about these boys, these young boys. They…
Just losing time, see. Did you ever work with a whole band, a young band, to try to teach the whole band together?
